title: The Croatian Army Crosses the Border
sources: ICTY Gotovina et al. Trial Judgment (IT-06-90-T), 15 April 2011
Balkan Battlegrounds, Vol. II (CIA, 2002), Ch. 15 (Operation Storm / Operation Mistral 2)
content:
With Operation Storm launching on 4 August 1995, Croatian Army Guards Brigades crossed the international border into Bosnia-Herzegovina to support HVO formations around Livno, Glamoč, and Bosansko Grahovo. Defence Minister Gojko Šušak coordinated directly with the HVO Main Staff in Mostar; the Tuđman presidential transcripts treat the Bosnian operations as an extension of Croatian state strategy, continuous with the recapture of the Krajina.

For Herceg-Bosna the arrival of regular HV formations on Bosnian soil posed a command question. Operation Mistral 2 of September 1995 — the drive that recaptured Šipovo, Mrkonjić Grad, and Jajce and brought Federation forces to the gates of Banja Luka — was substantially an HV operation with HVO support, executed under Croatian Army command. The HVO could subordinate itself to HV command and ride the offensive's momentum, run independent operations to assert a distinct Croat military identity, coordinate with the ARBiH under the Federation framework, or stand aside.

Historically the HVO accepted HV command in the western-Bosnian offensives, and the combined HV-HVO drive — paired with the ARBiH 5th and 7th Corps operations — collapsed the VRS position in western Bosnia and created the territorial facts that the Contact Group map and Dayton then ratified.

The posture recorded here conditions the scale and direction of the 1995 western-Bosnian offensive and the territorial map carried into Dayton.
